I honestly don't understand why people say this game is so amazing. It doesn't innovate on anything, it is glitchy, the controls feel dated, the graphics are average, the environments aren't the greatest, meshing and interaction suffer from many of the same issues as other games in this genre, and although there is some good missions and a decent story, most of the stuff in the game is pretty much another A to B to C style system with rewards--just like every game before it.

The menus and leveling system have more in common with 90s style dungeon crawlers than modern games, and the armor and weapons system could use some serious work--including getting rid of the annoying fucking degradation stuff they do.

It always felt like a more tedious version of the Elder Scrolls games to me. I mean, I like that a smaller company pumped out something decent, but it definitely isn't amazing by any stretch of the word, nor does it even attempt to improve on any of the faux pas of the genre or gaming in general.

It did something new with storytelling in this kind of game which is to make side quests as good or sometimes even better than the main quest. Also it did a very good job of making an open world game seem like a living world as opposed to a sandbox with triggered events. It still is basically a blend of an RPG and an open world game, but it doesn't feel like a typical open world game the way something like GTA5 or an Assassins creed game does.

The side quests are so memorable I can still picture a lot of them. Like the ancient Leshen bounty in the Skellige village, or the cat school Witcher who slaughters a village. Or the village turned into pigs. They finally captured the essence of the Witcher, which is a guy going from town to town solving mysteries and helping people, in a very memorable way.
